title: Map the current interactive command execution flow
description: Trace the current command lifecycle from dashboard interaction through API dispatch, broker or queue creation, Celery integration, worker execution, status updates, cancellation, retries, and infrastructure provisioning. Produce evidence-backed findings and identify contracts, coupling, failure modes, and migration decisions. This is a read-only investigation; it does not authorize implementation changes.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Investigation started. A read-only Coding Agent is tracing the dashboard-to-worker lifecycle, including dispatch, task state, Celery/SQS configuration, queue creation, worker startup, retries, cancellation, and status propagation. No source, infrastructure, or external state changes are authorized in this phase.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text:
## Investigation result

The current production route is dashboard Task creation → DynamoDB stream → dispatcher Lambda → Celery over SQS → long-lived command worker → GraphQL Task, TaskStage, and evaluation updates.

Verified findings:
- Celery is the active dispatch mechanism.
- The worker creates the SQS queue at runtime when absent; the queue is not provisioned by the current CDK stack.
- Celery creates its DynamoDB result-backend table at runtime when absent.
- Dashboard Task records and subscriptions are the user-visible state contract; the Celery result backend is secondary.
- The CDK stack creates an EC2 role/profile and SSM service document, but not the EC2 instance itself.
- Current durability gaps include early message acknowledgement, no renewable execution lease, no worker-side idempotent claim, non-atomic send/status recording, no deployment drain, and no proven dashboard cancellation flow.
- A shared queue uses consumer-side target rejection rather than broker-side routing.

The repository evidence was independently reviewed at the dashboard dispatch, dispatcher Lambda, Celery configuration, command task, infrastructure stack, and deployment restart boundaries. No files or external systems were changed.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Read-only command-flow investigation completed and independently reviewed. Replacement architecture and behavior specifications remain under the parent epic.
